column1: What does 'illegal' mean in LEGO building vernacular?
column2: A community-coined term for techniques that violate LEGO's official design standards/assembly guidelines—not a legal or safety term, but one describing connections that exceed the engineered deformation envelope of elements.

column1: What is the approximate interference dimension between stud outer diameter and tube inner diameter that creates LEGO's clutch power?
column2: Approximately 0.1 mm, maintained within tolerance bands of ±0.01 mm across millions of injection-molded parts.

column1: What are the key material properties of ABS plastic relevant to LEGO clutch mechanics?
column2: Glass transition temperature ~105°C, tensile/Young's modulus ~2.3 GPa, and yield strength ~40-50 MPa.

column1: What are the three mechanistic categories into which illegal LEGO techniques typically fall?
column2: 1) Connections inducing shear stress perpendicular to the intended load path, 2) assemblies constraining thermal expansion/contraction of the polymer matrix, 3) geometric configurations creating stress concentration points exceeding yield strength.

column1: What is the fundamental horizontal and vertical grid spacing in the LEGO system?
column2: 8.00 mm center-to-center horizontal stud spacing, and 3.2 mm vertical plate height increments (5 plates = 2 bricks = 9.6 mm).

column1: What three conditions define a 'legal' LEGO connection?
column2: 1) Respects integer multiples of the 8mm horizontal and 3.2mm vertical grid, 2) all studs fully seated without compression or angular deflection, 3) zero stored elastic energy in the assembly at rest.

column1: What is the 'elastic energy budget' invariant in geometric violations?
column2: Every illegal connection stores mechanical energy proportional to the deflection imposed and the spring constant of the deformed element; this energy must stay below the threshold causing permanent plastic deformation or fracture.

column1: What is the approximate friction coefficient for ABS-on-ABS contact in non-standard LEGO connections?
column2: Approximately 0.35, which combines with normal force from elastic compression to determine connection strength against shear and tensile loads.

column1: What is the 'tolerance accumulation principle' in illegal LEGO geometry?
column2: Manufacturing variance (e.g., ±0.02mm per critical feature) is not random noise but can stack cumulatively across multiple elements to create gaps or interference zones of 0.1mm or more, which builders exploit to force otherwise-forbidden connections.

column1: What is the central invariant every advanced illegal-technique practitioner must internalize regarding stress?
column2: The stress is always present even when invisible—an illegal connection doesn't violate physics, it transfers load onto a geometry never designed to carry it, accumulating microfatigue over repeated cycles.

column1: What visual/physical indicators signal that an illegal LEGO connection has exceeded the elastic limit?
column2: Stress whitening (milky surface discoloration from subsurface polymer crazing), tube deformation, stud mushrooming, and eventually fracture.

column1: What is the reversibility invariant for valid illegal (non-standard) connections?
column2: Connections must permit disassembly without requiring destructive force or inducing permanent plastic deformation, even when approaching ABS's ~40 MPa tensile yield strength.
